findings.headline: 6 of 21 documented 99214/99215 claims (29%) are documented below the billed level; peer rate is 3%
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 17.3% of 579 claims, against 4.1% expected after risk adjustment (z_adj 6.35). The excess shows up at every complexity level, including patients with 0–1 conditions. Random sample: 27 usable charts. 4 of 5 documented 99215 charts support a lower level. Note checks show little sign of inflated notes. The overpayment estimate is not reliable because only 5 charts fell in the 99215 stratum; do not quote a dollar figure. A certified coder should review this. It is not a finding.

findings.headline: Highest 99215 share (26.7% vs 5.0% expected), including about 20% on patients with 0–1 conditions, but the charts support the billed levels
findings.interpretation: 43 charts (random plus a targeted 99215 sample): only 2 (4.7%) were below the billed level. Note signals are somewhat high: 30% duplicate text, 21% signed late, 12% bulk-created and 14% paste-heavy in the audit trail. The review did not flag the notes as inflated. Notes that match the bill could still be inflated, so a coder should look at the audit-trail examples. Not referred for recovery.
